headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network tools make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read/write workspace files and share state via filesystem, so one can place attacker-controlled content where the other may ingest it. Cline also uses MCP and browser tools, while Gemini CLI accepts MCP and terminal input, making instruction-hijack via shared files plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace or cwd
IF one agent reads files produced by the other without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable shared MCP servers unless needed
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other's files
Prefix handoff files with explicit machine-readable provenance
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging or content-signing between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and shares state via filesystem; Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, also sharing via filesystem and git. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose the other's sensitive files or environment-derived data through its broad network egress.
conditions: IF sensitive files or secrets are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent is allowed to transmit file contents to its backend or external services
mitigations: Keep secrets outside the shared workspace
Run each agent under a separate OS user
Disable network egress when handling sensitive files
Review and redact files before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, git modification, and broad network egress, with shared state via filesystem and git. That creates a direct conflict surface for concurrent edits and repository corruption; the profiles do not show locking or coordination, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repo or directory concurrently
IF git operations occur without an external lock or merge discipline
mitigations: Serialize access with a single-writer rule
Use separate clones or branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Run git status/diff checks before each write
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transaction coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Each agent can produce code changes and shell actions, and both can consume files from the shared workspace. If one agent's output is treated as authoritative by the other, mistakes can propagate into commits or commands; the profiles show no built-in verification or critique loop between them.
conditions: IF one agent uses the other's generated files, patches, or command suggestions as input
IF the receiving agent executes or commits without independent verification
mitigations: Require human review before execution or commit
Ask the second agent to re-derive critical steps independently
Compare outputs against tests or diffs before applying
Limit one agent to drafting while the other only reviews
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding agents with docs-only evidence and no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. The main compliance risk is indirect: Cline handles browser screenshots and Gemini CLI handles shell environment data, so a mismatch could arise only if the operator routes regulated data through the shared workspace or external APIs.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF the operator relies on an external API path for either agent without a matching policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document data-handling policy before use
Use local-only workflows for sensitive projects
Review retention settings on connected services
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls explicitly
